data.name: Bulgaria
data.summary: Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026. It taxes residents' dividends at 5% and other income at a 10% flat rate. Gains on shares sold on EU/EEA regulated markets are exempt; gains realised on US exchanges are taxed at about 9% effective. There is no wealth tax, and transfers to children by gift or inheritance are tax-free.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Bulgarian tax residence: worldwide income at a 10% flat rate; dividends 5%.
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident through more than 183 days in any 12-month period, centre of vital interests in Bulgaria, or permanent address plus centre of vital interests.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on shares (and ETFs) disposed of on a regulated market in the EU/EEA are exempt (Personal Income Taxes Act, art. 13(1)(3)). Other gains on financial assets, including shares sold on US exchanges, are taxed at the 10% flat rate on the annual net result, with a 10% statutory deduction, so about 9% effective. Unlisted company shares: 10%. Real estate: one home held over 3 years plus up to two other properties held over 5 years per year are exempt; otherwise 10% on the gain less a 10% deduction.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: EU/EEA regulated-market disposals: exempt. Real estate exemptions per year: one residential property held >3 years and up to two other properties held >5 years (for Bulgarian and EU/EEA residents).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: The test is the trading venue, not the issuer: SAP sold on Xetra is exempt, sold on NYSE taxable. US exchanges and, since Brexit, the LSE do not qualify per secondary sources; PwC states the exemption was extended from 2021 to 'equivalent third-country' markets, but which markets count was not verified. Losses on financial assets offset only gains of the same year. From 1 Jan 2026 (State Gazette 113/2025) §1 item 11(a) of the PITA additional provisions covers disposals of shares, fund units, rights and government securities 'on a regulated market and/or a growth market', and new items 65-66 define these by reference to the CITA (§1 items 70-70a), which points to the Markets in Financial Instruments Act art. 152 (regulated markets) and to EU MiFID II growth markets. US exchanges are not MiFID regulated markets, so gains on US-listed shares sold there stay taxable (assumed).

sources.title: Capital Gains from Shares and ETFs - Reporting by Bulgarian Individuals (2026)
Закон за данъците върху доходите на физическите лица (consolidated, lex.bg)

open_questions: Whether a foreign (e.g. US) exchange can ever qualify: the 2026 definition refers to MFIA art. 152 (Bulgarian and EU/EEA regulated markets); art. 152 text not opened. We assume US exchanges do not qualify.
Taxation of gains on foreign real estate (treated like local real estate?) not verified.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Domestic listed (Bulgarian Stock Exchange regulated market): 0%. Foreign listed: 0.09 assumes a non-EU venue such as NYSE/Nasdaq (10% x 90% of gain); EU/EEA-venue holdings are 0%. Private business sale: 10% on the gain. Real estate local: 0 assumes a property held more than 5 years and within the two-property annual exemption; otherwise about 9%.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Individuals pay 10% on financial-asset gains regardless of frequency; trading organised as a sole-trader business would be taxed as business income at 10% plus social contributions (not verified).
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: No holding period for securities. Real estate: 3 years for one home, 5 years for up to two other properties.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents are taxed on worldwide gains, reported in the annual return.

dividends.summary: Dividends from Bulgarian and foreign companies are taxed at 5% (final). Foreign withholding tax is credited up to the Bulgarian tax, so foreign dividends that already bore 5% or more at source (e.g. 15% US treaty rate) normally owe no further Bulgarian tax.

sources.title: Bulgaria - Individual - Foreign tax relief and tax treaties

open_questions: Exact credit limitation formula for foreign dividends not read in the statute.
dividends.rate_basis: 5% final tax on dividends and liquidation proceeds; foreign dividends self-assessed at 5% with a per-country credit for foreign tax.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 5% WHT on dividends to non-residents (treaty reductions); exempt for EU/EEA resident companies except hidden profit distributions.
dividends.treaty_network: 71 double tax treaties, including the US.
dividends.holding_company_notes: 10% CIT and 5% dividend WHT (0% to EU/EEA companies) make Bulgaria a low-tax holding location; Pillar Two QDMTT applies to large groups.

wealth_tax.summary: Bulgaria has no net wealth tax and no levy on financial assets.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal real estate tax 0.01%-0.45% of the property's tax value, set by each municipality.

inheritance.summary: Inheritance tax is a municipal tax under the Local Taxes and Fees Act, but the surviving spouse and lineal heirs (children, grandchildren, parents) do not pay it (art. 31(2)). Gifts between lineal relatives and between spouses are also not taxed (art. 44(6)). Transfers from parents to children are therefore tax-free, both during life and on death.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Children: full exemption. For other heirs: BGN 250,000 (about EUR 127,800) per heir non-taxable, then 0.4%-0.8% for siblings and their children and 3.3%-6.6% for others, set by municipality.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Notary and registration fees apply to real estate transfers; not quantified. An inheritance declaration may still have to be filed with the municipality.

Oblagane na dareniyata po Zakona za mestnite danatsi i taksi

open_questions: Consolidated statute read from a private legal database, not the State Gazette; notary fee level not verified.
Art. 29(1) taxes worldwide estate for Bulgarian citizens and Bulgarian-situs property otherwise; irrelevant for children but relevant for other heirs.
inheritance.spouse_note: The surviving spouse does not pay inheritance tax, without limit of value (Local Taxes and Fees Act, art. 31(2)); gifts between spouses are also untaxed (art. 44(6)).
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax between lineal relatives or spouses (ZMDT art. 44(6)). Others: 0.4%-0.8% (siblings and their children) or 3.3%-6.6% (others).
inheritance.foreign_assets: Exemption for lineal heirs applies to all assets.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Scope: Bulgarian citizens on worldwide estate; foreign citizens on property in Bulgaria (ZMDT art. 29). Children exempt in any case.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if present more than 183 days in any 12-month period, if the centre of vital interests is in Bulgaria, or with a permanent address in Bulgaria combined with the centre of vital interests there. Treaties override.

routes.name: EU free movement
routes.requirements: EU/EEA/Swiss citizens may reside and register (details not separately verified).

routes.name: Long-stay visa D and residence permit
routes.requirements: Non-EU nationals need a type D visa and residence permit for a recognised purpose. A digital-nomad permit exists (funds of 50 gross minimum monthly salaries, one year, renewable once). Investment-based routes not verified.

corporate.summary: CIT 10% flat; Pillar Two (QDMTT, IIR, UTPR) for large groups. 5% dividend WHT to non-residents, exempt to EU/EEA companies.

income.name: Bulgaria

income_tax.summary: Flat 10% personal income tax on worldwide income of residents, with some exceptions. Employee contributions 10.58% social security plus 3.2% health (13.78% combined) on a maximum monthly insurance base of EUR 2,111.64 from 1 Jan to 31 Jul 2026 and EUR 2,300 from 1 Aug 2026; the recorded cap is the time-weighted annual figure (7 x 2,111.64 + 5 x 2,300 = EUR 26,281.48).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Freelancer insurance base: EUR 550.66 minimum (to 31 Jul) then EUR 620.20 (from 1 Aug), maximum as above. Rate: one secondary source gives 27.8% (31.3% with the optional illness and maternity fund) and elsewhere about 32-33%, so the recorded 27.8% is unverified. A 25% normative expense deduction for freelancers is commonly cited but was not confirmed in any opened source. PwC's other-taxes page (opened again 2026-10-15) gives freelancer minimum and maximum insurance bases but no freelancer contribution rate, and the NSSI site opened has none either.

regimes.name: Digital nomad residence permit (Foreigners Act Art. 24s)
regimes.description: Type D visa then one-year residence permit for third-country nationals who are remote employees, owners of more than 25% of a foreign company, or freelancers with at least one year of activity. Average annual gross income (the Act measures gross income) of at least 50 minimum monthly wages for the previous calendar year (EUR 27,533 on the 2025 wage; EUR 31,010 on the 2026 wage; practice unsettled). Work for Bulgarian clients prohibited; health insurance of at least EUR 30,000. Under 183 days and with the centre of vital interests abroad, remote income is generally not taxable in Bulgaria; a resident pays 10%.
regimes.duration_note: 1 year, renewable once; no path to permanent residence.
open_questions: Source is a consultancy blog; rules apply from 20 Dec 2025.
The minimum wage basis (2025 vs 2026) is unsettled.

rent_1bed_monthly.description: Average monthly rent for a standard furnished 1-bedroom, about BGN 1,170 (typical EUR 500-950), weighted toward non-central stock, per Investropa as of June 2026 (updated 5 Oct 2026); sources Numbeo, Imoti.info, Properties.bg.

rent_2bed_monthly.description: Average monthly rent for a good non-luxury 2-bedroom, about BGN 1,530 (typical EUR 650-1,400), scaled from 1- and 3-bedroom benchmarks, per Investropa, June 2026.

costs.notes: Publisher's estimate, not official statistics; euro values as stated by the source.

succession.name: Bulgaria
succession.summary: Children are guaranteed half of the estate with one child and two thirds with two or more, which a will cannot reduce. A foreign national resident can choose the law of their nationality under the EU Succession Regulation. Bulgaria has no trust law; foundations exist but only for non-profit purposes.
succession.reserved_share: Children: 1/2 of the estate with one child, 2/3 with two or more; spouse and parents also protected; Law on Inheritance (Закон за наследството) arts. 28-30. Fractions for spouse and parents not confirmed.
succession.foreign_law_note: Regulation 650/2012 art. 22 lets a person choose the law of their nationality; the reserved share of the chosen law then applies, not the Bulgarian one.
succession.trust_note: No trust law; no treaty recognition. Foundations exist under the Non-Profit Legal Entities Act 2000 for public or restricted private-benefit purposes, so a family foundation is heavily restricted.
open_questions: Reserved share of spouse and parents (Law on Inheritance art. 28 and following).
How far a foundation can serve a family under the Non-Profit Legal Entities Act.
Tax treatment of foreign trusts.

immigration.name: Bulgaria
immigration.summary: EU citizens only register. Non-EU citizens (US and others) can get permanent residence by investing about EUR 255,646 in a company that creates 10 jobs, or about EUR 511,000 in funds; digital nomads need about EUR 31,000 a year of foreign income. Citizenship by investment ended in 2022.
immigration.naturalisation: Typically a long-term or permanent residence permit held for at least 5 years, income or occupation, and Bulgarian language; 3 years in some cases (marriage to a Bulgarian citizen, a Bulgarian child per one source).
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: One source says Bulgaria allows it; another says naturalised citizens outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland must renounce. Treated as allowed pending confirmation.

routes.name: EU/EEA/Swiss free movement (registration)
routes.summary: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens may live in Bulgaria and register with the Migration Directorate after 3 months; permanent residence after 5 years.
routes.requirements: Valid ID or passport; worker, self-employed or economically inactive with resources and health cover. Permanent right after 5 years of continuous legal residence (Directive 2004/38). The Bulgarian 3-month registration procedure itself was not separately sourced.
routes.tax_note: Tax residence follows the 183-day or centre-of-vital-interests test.

sources.title: Your Europe: Residence rights in another EU country

routes.name: Residence by investment: Bulgarian company with 10 jobs
routes.summary: Permanent residence for investing about EUR 255,646 (BGN 500,000) in a Bulgarian company that creates and keeps 10 full-time jobs.
routes.requirements: Direct equity in an active Bulgarian company creating and maintaining at least 10 full-time jobs for Bulgarian citizens. Article 25 of the Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria Act with the Investment Promotion Act. Amount converted at the fixed rate 1.95583 BGN per EUR since euro adoption on 1 January 2026. Sources are secondary and one page marks the whole route 'in flux'.
routes.family: Spouse and children; one source adds dependent parents.
routes.tax_note: A permit does not make you tax resident.

sources.title: Bulgaria: permanent residence through company investment and ten jobs

routes.name: Residence by investment: regulated Bulgarian funds
routes.summary: Permanent residence for about EUR 511,000 (BGN 1,000,000) in licensed Bulgarian funds held for five years.
routes.requirements: Placement in government-licensed Bulgarian alternative investment funds or ETFs focused on domestic assets, held for 5 years. Sources quote BGN 1,000,000 (about EUR 511,292) or 'about EUR 512,000'. Article 25 of the Foreigners Act.
routes.tax_note: A permit does not make you tax resident.

routes.name: Residence by investment: real estate
routes.status_note: One 2026 guide says the direct real estate route closed in January 2025; another 2026 page still lists it at BGN 600,000. Treated as closed pending official confirmation.
routes.summary: A property purchase of BGN 600,000 (about EUR 307,000) was reported as a route, but is probably closed.
routes.requirements: Reported minimum BGN 600,000 with at least 75% own funds from abroad (one guide). Not confirmed.

routes.name: Digital nomad visa (type D) and residence permit
routes.summary: For remote workers earning about EUR 31,000 a year (50 monthly minimum wages) from outside Bulgaria; opened in December 2025.
routes.requirements: Income of 50 times the monthly minimum wage (about EUR 620 a month in January 2026, so about EUR 31,000 a year; adjusts with the wage; one source says about EUR 27,500). Remote work for a foreign employer or clients or own foreign company; freelancers need a year of foreign clients (one source). No work for Bulgarian employers or clients. Health insurance (EUR 30,000 or EUR 60,000 cover, sources differ). Type D visa abroad, then apply for a permit within 14 days of arrival. 1 year, extendable once for a year.
routes.tax_note: Bulgaria has a 10% flat tax on residents; 183 days makes you tax resident.

sources.title: Bulgaria's digital nomad visa (2026): the EUR 31K income rule

routes.name: Long-term residence for retirees / passive income (type D visa)
routes.summary: Retirees and others with stable foreign income can get a type D visa and annual long-term permit; the required income is not fixed in sources.
routes.requirements: Pension or passive income from abroad, Bulgarian health insurance (cover at least EUR 30,000), three months of pension statements, accommodation. Guides give conflicting income benchmarks (about USD 800 a month, or about BGN 5,000 a month), none from an official source.
routes.tax_note: Permit renewed annually per one guide.

routes.name: Work permits (single permit, EU Blue Card)
routes.summary: Non-EU workers need an employer, a work permit and a type D visa; the Blue Card applies to highly qualified roles.
routes.requirements: Employer-led; labour-market tests and quotas not researched in depth.
routes.physical_presence: Live in Bulgaria; no fixed day count sourced

routes.name: Citizenship by investment
routes.status_note: Discontinued in 2022 (reported March 2022); only residence by investment remains.
routes.summary: Bulgaria's fast-track citizenship for investors no longer exists.
routes.requirements: Closed. Sources agree it was abolished in 2022; details of the former terms were not researched.
